pull_requests.title: Map the PTCH1-specific Gorlin DOID to basal cell nevus syndrome 1
pull_requests.body:
Gorlin syndrome includes both PTCH1-related and SUFU-related disease. The current mapping treats the PTCH1 subtype as equivalent to the entire Gorlin family. This PR moves that exact match to MONDO's existing PTCH1 subtype.

| ID | Source label | Gene context | Relevant parent or scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| MONDO:0007187 | nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome | Includes PTCH1 and SUFU subtypes | Gorlin family; parent of basal cell nevus syndromes 1 and 2 |
| DOID:2512 | nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome | Includes PTCH1 and SUFU subtypes | Gorlin family; parent of nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndromes 1 and 2 |
| MONDO:0958174 | basal cell nevus syndrome 1 | PTCH1 | Nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome |
| DOID:0070365 | nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome 1 | PTCH1 | Nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome |
| MONDO:0958189 | basal cell nevus syndrome 2 | SUFU | Nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome |
| DOID:0070366 | nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome 2 | SUFU | Nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome |

Gene context comes from checked source definitions and subtype relationships, not from Boomer. Gene examples for a disease family are not an exhaustive list.

**Correction:** match the Disease Ontology PTCH1 subtype to MONDO's basal cell nevus syndrome 1, and keep the two broader Gorlin categories matched to each other. The subtype records agree on PTCH1 and OMIM:109400. The corresponding DOID subset provenance moves with the exact match.

**Why:** the SUFU subtype is another member of the Gorlin family, so the family and its PTCH1 subtype are not interchangeable. Both ontologies already make this distinction. A family with SUFU-related Gorlin syndrome was described by [Pastorino et al. (2009)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19533801/).

<details>
<summary>Boomer report, source checks, and validation</summary>

The [Gorlin report](https://github.com/monarch-initiative/dismech/blob/fbbfb73d5bc4f10ccb86d303c9fe13c271c746f1/analyses/boomer/remaining-low-confidence/Gorlin_Syndrome-alternatives.md) found two equally weighted, distinct solutions: one retained the exact match to the PTCH1 subtype; the other retained the exact match to the broader Gorlin category. The two mappings each had an input prior of 0.95. Because the input treats the DOID parent and child as distinct, both equivalences cannot hold together.

| Distinct solution | Exact match retained | Exact match rejected | Whole-solution posterior |
|---|---|---|---:|
| Saved best | MONDO Gorlin family ↔ DO PTCH1 subtype | MONDO Gorlin family ↔ DO Gorlin family | 0.337481 |
| Equally weighted alternative | MONDO Gorlin family ↔ DO Gorlin family | MONDO Gorlin family ↔ DO PTCH1 subtype | 0.337481 |

Only the differing choices are shown; other choices in these two complete solutions are identical. Both competing exact mappings had input prior 0.95; each had marginal posterior 0.487179. The best-versus-next-best confidence is 0.5. The gene and hierarchy evidence above determines the proposed correction.


Exhaustive enumeration found 384 consistent complete assignments. The two best assignments each had posterior probability 0.337481; the confidence comparing those two solutions was 0.5. These are model scores, not probabilities that the clinical classification is correct. The reason to choose this correction is the agreement of the genes, OMIM identifiers, and parent–child relationships in the source ontologies.

In the [checked DO source](https://github.com/DiseaseOntology/HumanDiseaseOntology/blob/ec05d8346757d228193d33e6ef7a565f430ebe39/src/ontology/doid.obo#L29346), DOID:0070365 specifies PTCH1 and MIM:109400 and is a child of DOID:2512. MONDO:0958174 has the matching gene and OMIM identifier and is a child of MONDO:0007187. The SUFU subtype already has its own mapping: MONDO:0958189 ↔ DOID:0070366.

Investigation and reproducible reports: https://github.com/monarch-initiative/dismech/pull/11728.

Validation: `make NORM` passed with local OWLTools and ROBOT, with no unrelated serialization changes. All six repository xref QC queries passed for the affected terms: xref syntax, xref and annotation prefixes, mapping precision, conflicting precision annotations, and exact-synonym consistency. The containerized full ontology test suite was not run locally (Docker is unavailable).

</details>

pull_requests.title: Move the PRAAS1 DOID mapping to the existing PRAAS1 subtype
pull_requests.body:
Proteasome-associated autoinflammatory syndrome (PRAAS) includes several genetic forms. The current mapping treats PRAAS1 as equivalent to the entire PRAAS family. This PR moves that exact match to MONDO's existing PRAAS1 term.

| ID | Source label | Gene context | Relevant parent or scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| MONDO:0009726 | proteosome-associated autoinflammatory syndrome | Multiple proteasome genes, including PSMB8 and POMP | Broader PRAAS family |
| DOID:0060913 | proteosome-associated autoinflammatory syndrome | Includes PSMB8 and POMP subtypes | Broader PRAAS family; parent of PRAAS1 and PRAAS2 |
| MONDO:0054698 | proteasome-associated autoinflammatory syndrome 1 | PSMB8; synonym includes digenic forms | Proteosome-associated autoinflammatory syndrome |
| DOID:0050553 | proteasome-associated autoinflammatory syndrome 1 | PSMB8; specified digenic forms involve PSMA3 or PSMB4 | Proteosome-associated autoinflammatory syndrome |
| DOID:0060914 | proteosome-associated autoinflammatory syndrome 2 | POMP | Proteosome-associated autoinflammatory syndrome |

Gene context comes from checked source definitions and subtype relationships, not from Boomer. Gene examples for a disease family are not an exhaustive list.

**Correction:** match the two PRAAS1 records to each other, and keep the two broader PRAAS categories matched to each other. The PRAAS1 records agree on OMIM:256040 and cover PSMB8-related disease and specified digenic forms. The corresponding DOID and DOID rare subset provenance moves with the exact match.

**Why:** PRAAS2, caused by POMP variants, is one example of disease within the broader family that is not PRAAS1. The [checked PRAAS2 record](https://github.com/DiseaseOntology/HumanDiseaseOntology/blob/ec05d8346757d228193d33e6ef7a565f430ebe39/src/ontology/doid.obo#L21955) makes that distinction explicit. Genetic heterogeneity across PRAAS was also demonstrated by [Brehm et al. (2015)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26524591/). Source spelling is retained in the table.

<details>
<summary>Boomer report, source checks, and validation</summary>

The [PRAAS report](https://github.com/monarch-initiative/dismech/blob/fbbfb73d5bc4f10ccb86d303c9fe13c271c746f1/analyses/boomer/remaining-low-confidence/Proteasome_Associated_Autoinflammatory_Syndrome-alternatives.md) found two equally weighted, distinct solutions: one retained the exact match to the broader PRAAS category; the other retained the exact match to PRAAS1. Both mappings had an input prior of 0.95. Because the input treats the DOID parent and child as distinct, both equivalences cannot hold together.

| Distinct solution | Exact match retained | Exact match rejected | Whole-solution posterior |
|---|---|---|---:|
| Saved best | MONDO PRAAS family ↔ DO PRAAS family | MONDO PRAAS family ↔ DO PRAAS1 | 0.352398 |
| Equally weighted alternative | MONDO PRAAS family ↔ DO PRAAS1 | MONDO PRAAS family ↔ DO PRAAS family | 0.352398 |

Only the differing choices are shown; other choices in these two complete solutions are identical. Both competing exact mappings had input prior 0.95; each had marginal posterior 0.487179. The best-versus-next-best confidence is 0.5. The gene and hierarchy evidence above determines the proposed correction.


Exhaustive enumeration found 96 consistent complete assignments. The two best assignments each had posterior probability 0.352398; the confidence comparing those two solutions was 0.5. These are model scores. The source definitions and matching OMIM identifiers establish which mapping belongs on which term.

The [checked DO source](https://github.com/DiseaseOntology/HumanDiseaseOntology/blob/ec05d8346757d228193d33e6ef7a565f430ebe39/src/ontology/doid.obo#L5524) defines DOID:0050553 as PRAAS1 caused by biallelic PSMB8 variants or specified digenic combinations involving PSMB8, and maps it to MIM:256040. It is a child of DOID:0060913, which maps to the OMIM phenotypic series PS256040. MONDO:0054698 already carries OMIM:256040, the PSMB8 relationship, and a synonym covering PRAAS1 and digenic forms. MONDO:0009726 carries OMIMPS:256040.

Historical CANDLE/JMP/Nakajo-Nishimura synonyms on the broader MONDO term remain for separate review; this PR corrects the DOID mapping and its subset provenance.

Investigation and reproducible reports: https://github.com/monarch-initiative/dismech/pull/11728.

Validation: `make NORM` passed with local OWLTools and ROBOT, with no unrelated serialization changes. All six repository xref QC queries passed for the affected terms: xref syntax, xref and annotation prefixes, mapping precision, conflicting precision annotations, and exact-synonym consistency. The containerized full ontology test suite was not run locally (Docker is unavailable).

</details>

pull_requests.title: Distinguish TPMT deficiency from broader poor thiopurine metabolism
pull_requests.body:
TPMT deficiency is one cause of poor thiopurine metabolism; NUDT15-related poor metabolism is another. The current mapping treats TPMT deficiency as equivalent to the broader category containing both causes. This PR keeps the TPMT-specific exact match and records that TPMT deficiency is narrower than the broader category.

| ID | Source label | Gene context | Relevant parent or scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| MONDO:0012503 | thiopurine S-methyltransferase deficiency | TPMT | Thiopurine metabolic disease |
| DOID:0061004 | poor metabolism of thiopurines 1 | TPMT | Poor metabolism of thiopurines |
| DOID:0060996 | poor metabolism of thiopurines 2 | NUDT15 | Poor metabolism of thiopurines |
| DOID:0080172 | poor metabolism of thiopurines | Includes TPMT and NUDT15 subtypes | Broader category containing both forms |

Gene context comes from checked source definitions and subtype relationships, not from Boomer. Gene examples for a disease family are not an exhaustive list.

**Correction:** keep TPMT deficiency equivalent to the TPMT-specific poor-metabolism subtype. Change its relationship to the broader poor-metabolism category from an exact match to “MONDO is narrower than the source.” Remove the broader identifier from the exact-match subset provenance and two exact-synonym citations; those synonyms retain their other sources.

**Why:** the broader category also contains NUDT15-related poor metabolism. Equating that whole category with TPMT deficiency loses the genetic distinction. The [CPIC thiopurine guideline update (PMID:41618934)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41618934/) also treats TPMT and NUDT15 separately.

<details>
<summary>Boomer report, source checks, and validation</summary>

The [TPMT report](https://github.com/monarch-initiative/dismech/blob/fbbfb73d5bc4f10ccb86d303c9fe13c271c746f1/analyses/boomer/remaining-low-confidence/Thiopurine_S-methyltransferase_Deficiency-alternatives.md) found two equally weighted, distinct solutions: one retained the exact match to TPMT-specific poor metabolism; the other retained the exact match to the broader category. Both mappings had an input prior of 0.95. Because the input treats the DOID parent and child as distinct, both equivalences cannot hold together.

| Distinct solution | Exact match retained | Exact match rejected | Whole-solution posterior |
|---|---|---|---:|
| Saved best | MONDO TPMT deficiency ↔ DO TPMT-specific subtype | MONDO TPMT deficiency ↔ DO broader poor-metabolism category | 0.374979 |
| Equally weighted alternative | MONDO TPMT deficiency ↔ DO broader poor-metabolism category | MONDO TPMT deficiency ↔ DO TPMT-specific subtype | 0.374979 |

Only the differing choices are shown; other choices in these two complete solutions are identical. Both competing exact mappings had input prior 0.95; each had marginal posterior 0.487179. The best-versus-next-best confidence is 0.5. The gene and hierarchy evidence above determines the proposed correction.


Exhaustive enumeration found 192 consistent complete assignments. The two best assignments each had posterior probability 0.374979; the confidence comparing those two solutions was 0.5. These are model scores. The correction follows the gene-specific definitions and DOID hierarchy.

In the [checked DO source](https://github.com/DiseaseOntology/HumanDiseaseOntology/blob/ec05d8346757d228193d33e6ef7a565f430ebe39/src/ontology/doid.obo#L22743), DOID:0061004 specifies TPMT and MIM:610460. Its parent, DOID:0080172, maps to MIM:PS610460 and also contains DOID:0060996, which specifies NUDT15 and MIM:616903. MONDO:0012503 already specifies TPMT, thiopurine S-methyltransferase activity, and OMIM:610460.

DOID:0080172 still has TPMT-specific exact synonyms. Those source synonyms do not make its broader category equivalent to TPMT deficiency. Removing that DOID identifier from the two synonym citations also avoids MONDO's QC conflict between exact synonyms and a non-exact mapping; the synonym text is unchanged.

Investigation and reproducible reports: https://github.com/monarch-initiative/dismech/pull/11728.

Validation: `make NORM` passed with local OWLTools and ROBOT, with no unrelated serialization changes. All six repository xref QC queries passed for the affected term: xref syntax, xref and annotation prefixes, mapping precision, conflicting precision annotations, and exact-synonym consistency. The containerized full ontology test suite was not run locally (Docker is unavailable).

</details>
